headline: A new law lets winners of the Patents for Humanity award pass their acceleration certificate to another party.
what_it_does: The Patents for Humanity program honors patent owners, applicants, and licensees who use their inventions to meet humanitarian needs. Winners receive a certificate that can speed up certain U.S. Patent and Trademark Office proceedings, such as a patent application. This law allows the holder of that certificate to transfer it to someone else.

who_it_affects.how: They can now transfer their acceleration certificate to another party instead of keeping it themselves.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations or individuals who might receive a transferred certificate
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to use a certificate that someone else earned to speed up certain Patent Office proceedings.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2021. The summary does not state a separate effective date.
